_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Kazakhstan covering Scythian/Saka nomads, Turkic khaganates, Silk Road cities, Mongol conquest, Kazakh Khanate (1465), Zhuz (horde) system, Russian colonisation, Soviet era (Virgin Lands, nuclear testing at Semipalatinsk), December 1986 protests, independence 1991, Nazarbayev era, capital move to Astana, oil-driven economy, and Tokayev reforms.

religion.note: Secular state; Islam among Kazakhs is traditionally moderate/nomadic-influenced; Congress of Leaders of World Religions hosted in Astana

ethnic_groups.name: Kazakh
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkic; three zhuz (hordes): Great (south), Middle (central/east), Little (west); nomadic pastoralist heritage; eagle hunting; yurt culture; percentage rising due to oralman (ethnic Kazakh returnee) policy

ethnic_groups.name: Russian
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern/eastern Kazakhstan; declining (was 37% at independence); Slavic; Orthodox; many emigrating; Cossack communities; Russian-language dominance in cities

ethnic_groups.name: Uzbek
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkestan/Shymkent; Turkic; cross-border with Uzbekistan; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Ukrainian
ethnic_groups.notes: Soviet-era settlers; northern oblasts; declining; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Uyghur
ethnic_groups.notes: Almaty region; Turkic; cross-border with Xinjiang, China; some separatist sentiment concerns

ethnic_groups.name: German
ethnic_groups.notes: Deported from Volga 1941; was 6% at independence; most repatriated to Germany (Aussiedler); Karaganda area

ethnic_groups.name: Korean (Koryo-saram)
ethnic_groups.notes: Deported from Soviet Far East 1937 by Stalin; ~100,000; well-integrated; farming/business

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Dungan, Chechen, Kurdish, Polish, Belarusian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Diverse Soviet deportee communities; Dungan (Chinese Hui Muslims); Meskhetian Turks; total 130+ ethnicities; 'laboratory of inter-ethnic harmony' (official narrative)

independence.from: Soviet Union (last republic to declare independence)

country_profile.notes_unique: World's largest landlocked country (9th overall); Baikonur Cosmodrome (leased to Russia); Tengiz/Kashagan oil fields; former Soviet nuclear test site (Semipalatinsk, 456 tests); voluntarily gave up nuclear weapons; apple originated here (alma = apple, Almaty = city of apples)

trade.notes: World's largest uranium producer; major oil exporter (Kashagan, Tengiz); Caspian transit hub; EAEU membership; growing China trade.

infrastructure.notes: BRI key transit corridor; Belt & Road railway connections; Nurly Zhol infrastructure program; Caspian oil pipelines (CPC, BTC); vast distances challenge connectivity.

governance_indices.notes: Tokayev reforms post-2022; reduced presidential term; bicameral parliament; Nazarbayev legacy; high state control over economy and media.

country_profile.national_motto: Let the sky be clear, let all peoples live in peace

geography.terrain: Vast flat steppe; semi-desert and desert; mountainous in east and southeast; Caspian Sea coast west
geography.notes: Largest landlocked country; 9th largest globally; Baikonur Cosmodrome (leased to Russia); Aral Sea environmental catastrophe; vast oil/gas reserves in Caspian region.

economy_extended.notes: Central Asia's largest economy; oil-dependent (Kashagan, Tengiz fields); Astana International Financial Centre; rare earth minerals; grain exporter; Chinese BRI corridor.

health.notes: Soviet-era hospital infrastructure; mandatory health insurance since 2020; high TB rates for upper-middle income; Aral Sea region health crisis (respiratory, cancer).

food_agriculture.notes: Major wheat exporter; 6th globally; vast steppe grazing lands; horse culture; Virgin Lands Campaign legacy; growing organic sector.

security_stability.notes: Stable authoritarian governance; Jan 2022 Almaty unrest led to CSTO intervention; hosts Baikonur; nuclear-weapon-free since 1995; strategic buffer Russia-China.

environment_climate.notes: Aral Sea catastrophe among worst environmental disasters; coal-dependent power generation; steppe ecosystem; saiga antelope conservation; Semipalatinsk nuclear test site legacy.

demographics_extended.notes: Multi-ethnic (Kazakh 70%, Russian 15%+); Russification legacy; Kazakh language promotion; Bolashak scholarship program; growing urbanization.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Central Asia's largest economy; world's 9th largest country; major oil/uranium producer.

world_heritage_sites: Saryarka – Steppe and Lakes of Northern Kazakhstan
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: Kazinform (state); Tengrinews (online); Khabar TV; limited press freedom; Russian and Kazakh language media.
cultural_heritage.notes: Largest landlocked country; nomadic Turkic-Mongol heritage; Soviet legacy; Baikonur Cosmodrome; rapid modernization under Nazarbayev.

energy.notes: Major oil producer (Kashagan, Tengiz, Karachaganak); world's largest uranium producer; Baikonur Cosmodrome; coal-dependent electricity generation.

human_rights_gender.notes: Authoritarian governance; 2022 Bloody January protests (Almaty); ethnic Kazakh/Russian tensions; limited political pluralism.

legal_system.notes: Supreme Court; Constitutional Council; heavy executive influence; Astana International Financial Centre uses English common law.

tourism.notes: Growing ecotourism; ski resorts (Shymbulak); Silk Road heritage; visa-free for 77 countries.

transport.notes: Trans-Aral and Trans-Caspian railway links; Khorgos Gateway (China–Kazakhstan dry port); vast distances between cities; Air Astana national carrier.

current_leader.name: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Amanat party; career diplomat; succeeded Nazarbayev; January 2022 unrest (Bloody January); broke with Nazarbayev; 'New Kazakhstan' reforms; CSTO called in Russian troops

former_leaders.name: Nursultan Nazarbayev
former_leaders.notes: First president; 'Elbasy' (Leader of the Nation); 29-year rule; moved capital to Astana (renamed Nur-Sultan 2019-2022, reverted to Astana); oil wealth; authoritarian; personality cult; stripped of powers after January 2022 unrest
